record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Computational Geometry
record.original_question: Given a finite family D of unit disks in the plane and two points s and t not covered by any disk, define the annular-domain barrier-resilience problem as finding an s-t curve in the plane that touches as few disks of D as possible, equivalently removing as few disks as possible so that an s-t curve avoids all remaining disks. Determine the computational complexity of this problem for disks or unit disks in the annular domain: is there a polynomial-time algorithm, or is the problem NP-hard?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let D be a finite family of closed unit disks in the Euclidean plane, and let s, t be two points of the plane not contained in any disk of D. The barrier-resilience problem asks for a continuous curve from s to t in the plane that intersects (touches) the minimum possible number of disks of D; equivalently, it asks for a minimum-cardinality subfamily D' ⊆ D such that there exists an s-t curve avoiding every disk in D \ D'.

Consider the "annular-domain" variant in which the ambient region is restricted to a closed planar annulus A (the region between two concentric circles), the disks of D lie in A, and s and t lie on the two distinct boundary circles of A; admissible curves are those contained in A. 

Determine the computational complexity of the annular-domain barrier-resilience problem. Specifically: is there a polynomial-time algorithm for the problem when D consists of arbitrary disks, and when D consists of unit disks, or is the problem NP-hard in either case?
artifact.status_search_result: The complexity of barrier resilience for unit disks (and disks) in the plane is widely reported as an open problem; FPT algorithms and approximation results are known, and NP-hardness has been established only for other barrier shapes (line segments, near-square rectangles, certain fat regions). No source found resolves the annular-domain restriction, which is also stated as open.

status_evidence.title: Barrier resilience - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known whether it has a fully polynomial time solution. The corresponding problem for barriers of some other shapes ... is known to be NP-hard.
status_evidence.claim: Complexity for unit disks remains open; only FPT and approximation results exist.

status_evidence.title: On the Complexity of Barrier Resilience for Fat Regions and Bounded Ply
status_evidence.snippet: Barrier resilience for unit disks and fat regions: FPT algorithms; NP-hardness for related variants.
status_evidence.claim: State of the art shows the unit-disk case (and its annular restriction) is not known to be polynomial nor NP-hard.
